```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


### Part A: Importing and Inspecting a CSV

```{r}
# A1
emp_df <- read.csv("employees.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# A2
str(emp_df)
print(head(emp_df, 5))
print(summary(emp_df))

# A3
cat("Rows:", nrow(emp_df), "\n")
cat("Columns:", ncol(emp_df), "\n")
print(sapply(emp_df, class))

# A4
cat("Mean salary:", mean(emp_df$salary), "\n")
cat("Max age:", max(emp_df$age), "\n")
print(table(emp_df$department))

```

### Part B: Creating Data Frames
```{r}
# B1
new_hires <- data.frame(
  emp_id        = 21:23,
  name          = c("Uma", "Victor", "Wen"),
  department    = c("HR", "IT", "Sales"),
  sex           = c("F", "M", "F"),
  age           = c(28L, 37L, 33L),
  salary        = c(45000L, 83000L, 60000L),
  years_service = c(2L, 9L, 6L),
  rating        = c(3L, 4L, 5L),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

print(new_hires)

# B2
emp_all <- rbind(emp_df, new_hires)
print(dim(emp_all))

# B3
emp_all$bonus <- round(emp_all$salary * 0.05)

```


### Part C: Subsetting 

```{r}
# C1
print(emp_all[1:5, c("name", "salary")])

# C2
print(emp_all[emp_all$salary > 70000, ])

# C3
print(subset(emp_all,
             department == "IT" & years_service >= 5,
             select = c(name, years_service, salary)))

# C4
older_idx <- which(emp_all$age > 50)
print(older_idx)
print(emp_all$name[older_idx])

# C5
print(head(emp_all[, -c(1, which(names(emp_all) == "bonus"))], 3))

# C6
print(emp_all$salary[emp_all$name == "Mia"])

```



### Part D: Factors

```{r}
# D1
emp_all$department <- factor(emp_all$department)
emp_all$sex        <- factor(emp_all$sex)
print(levels(emp_all$department))
print(levels(emp_all$sex))

# D2
print(table(emp_all$department))
print(table(emp_all$department, emp_all$sex))

# D3
emp_all$rating_level <- factor(emp_all$rating,
                               levels = 1:5,
                               labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"),
                               ordered = TRUE)
print(table(emp_all$rating_level))

# D4
for (d in levels(emp_all$department)) {
  m <- mean(emp_all$salary[emp_all$department == d])
  cat(d, ":", round(m), "\n")
}

```


### Part E: Conditional Statements

```{r}
# E1
emp_all$salary_band <- ifelse(emp_all$salary >= 70000, "High",
                       ifelse(emp_all$salary >= 50000, "Medium", "Low"))
print(table(emp_all$salary_band))

# E2
emp_all$level <- ifelse(emp_all$years_service >= 8, "Senior", "Junior")
print(table(emp_all$level))

# E3
raise_pct <- function(rating) {
  if (rating == 5) {
    0.10
  } else if (rating == 4) {
    0.07
  } else if (rating == 3) {
    0.04
  } else {
    0
  }
}
emp_all$raise      <- sapply(emp_all$rating, raise_pct)
emp_all$new_salary <- round(emp_all$salary * (1 + emp_all$raise))
print(head(emp_all[, c("name", "rating", "raise", "new_salary")], 5))

# E4
total <- sum(emp_all$new_salary)
if (total < 1600000) {
  print("Budget OK")
} else {
  print("Over budget")
}
print(total)

```


### Part E: Conditional Statements

```{r}
# F1
print(sort(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5])
print(sort(emp_all$name)[1:5])

# F2
by_salary <- emp_all[order(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE), ]
print(head(by_salary[, c("name", "department", "salary")], 5))

```
